newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan trade surplus rises 6.5 pct in February.
newsitem.headline: Japan trade surplus rises 6.5 pct in February.

text.p: Japan's customs-cleared trade surplus rose 6.5 percent in February from a year earlier to 686.72 billion yen, the first rise in over two years, the Finance Ministry said on Monday.

The trade surplus with the United States, often a source of trade friction, rose 12.3 percent in February from a year earlier to 407.35 billion yen. The figures were not adjusted for seasonal factors.
At Monday's exchange rate of around 124 yen to the dollar, the overall customs-cleared trade surplus was $5.53 billion, while the surplus with the United States was $3.28 billion.

Economists' forecasts for the overall February trade surplus had ranged from 630 billion yen ($5.08 billion) to 831.3 billion yen ($6.70 billion). There was a surplus in February 1996 of 648.0 billion yen ($5.22 billion).
Many economists had expected a rise in the surplus as the weakening of the yen has recently accelerated Japan's exports while putting a brake on imports.
In the first 20 days of February, Japan's trade surplus had risen 53.3 percent from the same period a year earlier.
